summary: TLS handshake failures to control plane after enabling AWS PrivateLink due to split-horizon DNS aliasing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer enabled an AWS PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoint) to reach Redwood control plane from their VPC and on-prem network. After enabling the endpoint and a Route 53 private hosted zone, their application started failing TLS handshakes to api.redwood-inference.com.

Impact:
- All control-plane API requests from FinLedger's prod environment to api.redwood-inference.com in us-east-1 are failing TLS validation.
- Attempts to create new inference jobs and token refreshes are failing; customer reports degraded production traffic and automated retries do not recover.
- Error surfaces in app servers: "tls: certificate is not valid for requested name" and connection resets during TLS handshake.

Environment:
- Customer: FinLedger Inc (private tier)
- VPCs: vpc-0a1b2c3d (us-east-1) with interface endpoint vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a (com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com)
- Route 53: Private hosted zone created for redwood-inference.com in the customer's account
- Region: us-east-1
- Client stack: Go HTTP client + SNI enforced by client libs

Timeline / Observed behavior:
- 2026-03-09 10:12 UTC: Customer created interface endpoint for com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com and attached security groups.
- 2026-03-09 10:20 UTC: Customer created a private hosted zone redwood-inference.com with a CNAME record mapping api.redwood-inference.com -> vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com
- 2026-03-10 01:05 UTC: Customer apps started returning TLS validation errors; initial support ticket opened.

Steps to reproduce (customer environment):
1) From an app host inside their VPC: dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @10.0.0.2 (their resolver) -> returns "10.10.5.12" (private ENI IP of the interface endpoint).
2) curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:10.10.5.12 https://api.redwood-inference.com/health 2>&1 -> TLS handshake fails with certificate name mismatch.
3) openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -showcerts -> server cert CN/SAN contains "vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com", not api.redwood-inference.com.

Debug logs / evidence collected:
- dig output (customer resolver): "10.10.5.12" (matches interface endpoint ENI).
- openssl s_client shows server cert: subject CN=vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com; SANs do NOT include api.redwood-inference.com.
- tcpdump on host shows ClientHello SNI=api.redwood-inference.com and Server Certificate for vpce-... (mismatch).
- Support-side confirmation: public DNS resolves api.redwood-inference.com -> our public IPs; certificate served by our public LB includes api.redwood-inference.com in SAN.

Initial hypothesis:
- Customer created a private hosted zone or DNS override that maps api.redwood-inference.com to the VPCE interface IPs. The PrivateLink interface endpoint is terminating TLS with a certificate that lists the VPCE DNS name (vpce-...) as the certificate identity, not the public hostname. Because the clients request api.redwood-inference.com via SNI, TLS validation fails.
- This is a split-horizon DNS misconfiguration on the customer side, not a platform bug. The PrivateLink endpoint alias and the certificate presented by the endpoint are not compatible with the customer's DNS aliasing approach.

Workarounds and recommended remediation provided to customer so far:
- Immediate workaround (customer): add an explicit host override in /etc/hosts or container DNS to point api.redwood-inference.com to our public control-plane IPs so TLS certs match (not ideal for traffic routing). Example: curl --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:34.201.12.34 https://api.redwood-inference.com/health
- Preferred long-term remediation: remove the private hosted zone or CNAME mapping for api.redwood-inference.com. Instead, configure PrivateLink using an alias record that preserves the original hostname and ensure the endpoint is set up with a certificate that includes api.redwood-inference.com (requires coordination with infra; see runbook).
- Alternative: use SNI override on the client to accept the vpce-... certificate name (only if customer controls TLS validation behavior and accepts risk).

Next steps assigned:
- Support: Confirm whether the customer intended to route control-plane traffic over PrivateLink. If yes, coordinate with Infra/Platform to evaluate whether we can provision a PrivateLink-compatible cert chain or recommend a supported DNS pattern. (Assigned: Liam Ortega)
- Engineering/Infra: Review PrivateLink interface endpoint configuration and whether our endpoint can present a certificate containing api.redwood-inference.com for customer-managed endpoints or whether we must document this incompatibility. (Linked: INT-4389)
- Customer: Evaluate removing the private hosted zone and use Route 53 resolver rules to forward only specific suffixes to the endpoint, or accept the temporary /etc/hosts workaround.

Impact statement for internal stakeholders:
- Production outage for FinLedger's inference control-plane integration. Customer blocked on job creation and token refresh flows. Potential SLA breach if unresolved by sla_due_at.

Attachments / evidence files stored in ticket:
- tcpdump snippet (pcap) uploaded to ticket
- openssl output pasted into ticket notes
- dig outputs and private hosted zone screenshot provided by customer
comments: 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): First response sent to customer asking for dig output and openssl s_client output. Requested VPCE ID and private hosted zone name.

2026-03-10 03:40 UTC - FinLedger (Customer): Provided dig results showing api.redwood-inference.com -> 10.10.5.12 and screenshot of private hosted zone redwood-inference.com with CNAME to vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com.

2026-03-10 11:05 UTC - Liam Ortega (Support): Reproduced openssl s_client against provided IP; confirmed server cert CN=vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com. Hypothesis posted and INT-4389 opened to review PrivateLink cert options.

2026-03-11 09:12 UTC - Infra (Engineering): Acknowledged INT-4389; noted PrivateLink interface endpoints are managed by customer account; we cannot change the endpoint certificate in customer account. Suggested doc updates to PrivateLink runbook to call out split-horizon DNS caveat.

2026-03-11 14:20 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Shared mitigation steps with customer and requested confirmation if they can remove the private hosted zone. Customer trialing /etc/hosts workaround and will update by 2026-03-12.

2026-03-12 16:45 UTC - FinLedger (Customer): Confirmed temporary /etc/hosts workaround restored traffic for one of their app clusters. They will evaluate full DNS change this week and asked for recommended best practices documentation.
